newsitem.title: USA: American Home sees $0.09 97 EPS dilution.
newsitem.headline: American Home sees $0.09 97 EPS dilution.

text.p: American Home Products Corp said on Tuesday it expected its acquisition of the remaining 40 percent of Genetics Institute Inc to be dilutive by $0.09 a share in 1997.
The company expects to see the earnings per share dilution "lessening" in 1998 and 1999, an American Home spokesman said.
"It should be accretive after that," the spokesman said.
Pharmaceutical industry analysts had expected American Home to earn $3.42 a share in 1997, according to First Call. The consensus estimate for 1996 is for $2.95 a share.
Earlier, American Home it was excising its option to buy the 40 percent interest in Genetics Institute Inc that it did not already own for about $1.0 billion.

Alex. Brown analyst Kevin Tang said American Home would not have exercised the option and accepted the earnings dilution if it did not believe Genetics Institute's product pipeline would eventually yield dividends.
"We think it's a huge testiment to the strength of the product pipeline" at Genetics Institute, Tang said.
Other analysts were taking a wait-and-see attitude. "We'll see how the products work out in 1998," said independent pharmaceutical industry analyst Hemant Shah.
Last week a U.S. Food and Drug Administration advisory panel recommended the agency approve for marketing Genetics Institute's BeneFix blood-clotting therapy for treating hemophilia B.

Genetics Institute said on Tuesday it planned to file its Neumega drug for stimulating the growth of platelets, with the FDA before the end of 1996. Tang said he thought the drug could be on the market in 1997.
The company is also testing IL-12, a cellular immune activator, in cancer and HIV-infected patients, and BMP-2, a bone growth factor.
